usageNotes: Use this to remove a custom (e.g. Let's Encrypt or manually uploaded) TLS certificate from a PDM node and immediately replace it with a freshly generated self-signed certificate. The operation is synchronous and returns null on success; the web UI and API become reachable again without a service restart. Requires the System.Modify privilege on the calling token or user.

examples.summary: Revert pdm-node1 to a self-signed certificate after a bad custom cert upload

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes the current custom certificate and its associated private key, replacing them with a new self-signed certificate; any browser or client trust pinned to the previous certificate will immediately fail until re-accepted.
tips: The 'restart' query parameter is accepted for UI compatibility but has no effect — no service restart is triggered.
After this call completes, clients connecting to the node's web UI will receive an untrusted certificate warning until a new custom cert is uploaded or trust is re-established.
Use 'localhost' as the node value only when calling from the node itself; always use the real node name when targeting a remote node.
